"And that part is right here, I seee."
"But what is this land? It's like{n} the inside of a machine... no,{n} it IS a machine, through and through."
"There's no sign of anyone here. This{n} machine is all rusty, too. It looks like{n} it hasn't moved in hundreds of yeaars."
"Hundreds? No, far more than that.{n} This ground is like titanium, but{n} it's unlike any metal we know."
"How can you teeell?"
"I can tell by our footsteps. Light,{n} hard, and tougher than any alloy. Maybe{n} this is ancient civilization work, too."
"At a low estimate, I'd say a few{n} thousand years have gone by..."
"According to Special Service HQ's{n} map, this plateau half collapsed, and{n} only one part of it is left..."
"And that part is right here."
"Still, this is an awfully{n} strange place, isn't iiit?"
"Iron, gears, screws... It's just like{n} some sort of workshop, isn't iiit?"
"Yeah, like the inside of a clock."
"Oh myyy, then you can tell the time{n} whenever you like here.{n} What a very handy plaace!"
"Are you stupid?"
"...I'm sorryyy."
"Oh myy? There seems to be a boy out{n} in this lonely plaace? And he{n} doesn't look like a soldier, eitheer."
"No, never let your guard down.{n} Going by age, I'm not much different{n} from that kid over there myself."
"Hello there."
"Oh, yes, yes, hellooo."
"You two are a truly lovely work of art.{n} One finished whole made of two.{n} An imbalance of clashing light and dark."
"Huuh?"
"He's spouting weird stuff{n} right off the bat."
"So, who are you?"
"So, why are you here?"
"What do you mean by that?"
"He's spouting weird stuff{n} right off the bat."
"Um, excuse me, buut..."
"Who might you beee?"
"Why are you heere?"
"What does that meaan?"
"So, who are you?"
"If humans are to call me something,{n} Ymir. Still, names to tell each{n} individual apart were a fine invention."
"So, why are you here?"
"The meaning of that question is{n} vague. I cannot answer it, and if I{n} did, it would be of little use to you."
"What's that supposed to mean?"
"Adding another meaning to a meaning{n} is a bad habit of humans.{n} I meant exactly what the words say."
"And who might you be, I wondeer?"
"If humans must call me something:{n} Ymir. Names are a useful thing{n} for telling each individual apart."
"Why are you here, I wondeer?"
"The meaning of that question is{n} vague. I cannot answer it, and if I{n} did, it would be of little use to you."
"What do you mean by thaat?"
"Adding another meaning to a meaning{n} is a bad habit of humans.{n} I meant exactly what the words say."
"Tch, what's all this babbling about?{n} Good grief. Is this brat{n} cracked in the head or what?"
"U-ummm, I haven't the faintest{n} idea what you're talking abouut?"
"Pleease look? Over there... isn't that{n} the boy we met the other daaay?"
"Tch... something's fishy here."
"Hello. We meet again."
"Yeees, so it seeems."
"Look. It's that brat again..."
"It certainly seems thaat way.{n} Is this a coincidence too, I wondeer?"
"Who knows..."
"Good day. We meet again."
"Hey, you, brat. Why have you been{n} tailing us this whole time?"
"Following you? No, you are mistaken.{n} I am the one who bears the name Ymir.{n} Your guide, so to speak."
"A guide?"
"Guide us to what?"
"What do you mean?"
"Don't screw with me!"
"A guide, you saay?"
"A guide to whaat?"
"What do you meaan?"
"How interestiing."
"And what is it you're guiding us to?"
"Not a road in the physical sense.{n} I show all living things{n} the direction toward the future."
"Heh, that makes no damn sense."
"And what's that supposed to mean?"
"Meaning is what one perceives after{n} thinking. If thought is the essence of{n} humans, you too must think for yourself."
"Heh, mind your own business."
"Heh, don't screw with me!"
"By arriving at an answer like that,{n} you make the limits of your thinking{n} all the clearer to see."
"Haah? What the hell are you on about?{n} You got a screw loose somewhere{n} in that head of yours?"
"What will you be guiding us tooo?"
"Not a road in the physical sense.{n} I show all living things{n} the direction toward the future."
"R-riight...?"
"What does that meaan?"
"Meaning is what one perceives after{n} thinking. If thought is the essence of{n} humans, you too must think for yourself."
"Yees... I'm sooorry..."
"What an interesting answeer."
"'Interesting' is a perception, too.{n} By that perception and by feeling, you{n} strive to make sense of the baffling."
"Oh myyy? That boy from before{n} is standing right over theeere?"
"A guide... that's what he said."
"Could this mean that we're the ones{n} walking to wherever that brat{n} happens to be?"
"Surely not...?"
"Hello there."
"Yeees, hellooo!"
"Hello. We really do meet often."
"But is this a coincidence, I wondeer?"
"Who knows..."
"This land is where the machine stopped.{n} Its gears will never turn again, and{n} no pleasant ring of metal is heard."
"What's this one babbling about?"
"Obviously. A machine that was built{n} will stop moving someday.{n} However perfectly it was made."
"That can't be helped, can iiit?"
"Machines do stop somedaaay. The{n} grandfather clock at my house often{n} stopped when its spring ran down."
"Yes, a machine stops someday.{n} It is the same with humans. They lose{n} their functions and, in time, rot away."
"That's the law of nature."
"But people give birth to children.{n} Machines don't make children, do theey?"
"Copying oneself is a simple task.{n} And you people say that machines,{n} unlike humans, do not think."
"Yet human thought is machine-like too:{n} chemicals produced by outside stimuli,{n} mosaic fragments born of a network."
"You're saying machines and humans are{n} the same? But humans made machines.{n} So who made humans, then?"
"Don't tell me it was God.{n} Say that, and this turns{n} into a joke on the spot."
"Who made them is not the issue. I am{n} speaking of how humans function.{n} That is: a human, too, is a machine."
"Heh! There's just no pinning down{n} anything you say. That's nothing{n} but playing with words."
"Still, humans are strange beings.{n} They kill their own kind, and at{n} times even end their own lives..."
"Yes, you people call it suicide."
"Some creatures act in similar ways,{n} but they are driven by necessity:{n} a system for the species to survive."
"But humans favor death without order.{n} Runaway desire kills their own kind;{n} a surge of emotion kills the self..."
"At times, in humanitarianism's name,{n} they themselves hand down to posterity{n} disease factors that ought to die out."
"That is the weakening of a species."
"The devilish side that kills its kind.{n} The god-playing side that keeps{n} its kind alive."
"A heart that has lost its way."
"Truly a being filled with chaos."
"Look at this island of turmoil, both of{n} you. It is the world in miniature, or{n} the inner landscape of humankind."
"The world's turmoil has its{n} origin in the heart."
"The heart is where sin begins:{n} the wellspring of original sin."
"So if you took the heart out of humans,{n} they'd be saved a little? Is that{n} what you're saying?"
"But having a heart is what makes{n} us human."
"Love and friendship, which only humans{n} have... wonderful feelings like those{n} all exist thanks to the heart."
"Well now, I wonder. But there is{n} something I take great interest in."
"A new, autonomous being with a human's{n} power of thought and functions, that{n} acts only on what logic supports..."
"Tch, the brat's vanished!"
"But it bothers me."
"What does?"
"If the heart is the source of evil,{n} are humans, who have hearts,{n} evil itself?"
"Heh. Don't be stupid."
"What's evil and what's good, anyway?{n} Those are only value judgments the{n} human heart came up with to begin with."
"Is killing your own kind evil?{n} Is killing yourself evil?{n} Is destroying nature evil?"
"Then why is that evil?"
"Nobody in this world can explain it.{n} Because the idea of good and evil{n} is a terribly vague thing."
"Don't let something that vague{n} tie you down."
"Trust the judgment your own heart makes."
"Don't let other people's words{n} lead you astray."
"You're right..."
"The machine's started moving!?{n} No way! It has no power source!"
"Look! That iron wall over there!"
"Gi-gi... gi-gi-gi-gi... gi-gi..."
"A machine... with a human face!?"
"But I can see something like a heart?{n} This is no ordinary machine!"
"Still, it's way too big! I haven't laid{n} eyes on a monster this huge since{n} I came to this island!"
"Could it be!?"
"Could this be another of the ancient{n} weapons called Machine Gods that{n} appeared a hundred years ago!?"
"No. A hundred years ago, at least,{n} no Machine God had a shape like that.{n} Not in any army record photo I've seen!"
"Then what?"
"A machine monster with a human face..."
"Call it a Machine Man, I guess!?"
"A Machine Man..."
"Isn't this thing a pure machine!? Or is{n} this ground of steel the real body{n} of the monster in front of us!?"
"Is this a Machine Man... too!?"
"A giant human machine run by gears.{n} A Clockwork Machine Man,{n} you might call it!"
"What's that statue?"
"The ring's making a sound?"
"Is this statue resonating with the{n} ring I got at Special Service HQ,{n} the 'Twelve Keys' ring or whatever?"
"What's that light!?"
"A beam of light with insane power!{n} It's like that 'death ray' thing{n} the Romulus army was researching!"
"A giant machine foe called Machine Man.{n} But could even a monster like that{n} have such a thing as a heart?"
"Don't think about pointless stuff!{n} Right now, taking it down comes first!"
"Aim for the spinning gear in the{n} middle! That looks like its main body!{n} And watch out for the death ray!"
"We're aiming for the spinning geaar!{n} Please watch out for the light attack!{n} Don't bunch up in one place!"
"Let us go, Mr. {hero:6}!"

"Yes!"
